In the economy, money assumes specific functions, making it unique as a commodity, serving as a medium of exchange, store of value, and unit of account. The narrowest definition of the money supply is M1. The measure M2 is broader. Checking accounts allow banks and other financial institutions to create money by making loans to economic agents. The key is the existence of fractional reserve banking, which means banks are required to keep a fraction of the deposits in reserve. They can lend the rest. By expanding or reducing loan activity, the banking system alters the money supply according to the money multiplier. But individual banks create money by lending their excess reserves, the funds held by banks that exceed the minimum reserve requirement. Although the banking system creates money and facilitates economic growth, several factors constrain the process. Digital currency, an example of fiat money, facilitates an electronic form of exchange. The types of digital currency are central bank digital currency, cryptocurrency, stablecoins, and virtual currency.
